generator: make-mixes.sh (espeak-ng 1.51 en-us narration + ffmpeg 6.1.1 synthesised chord/pink-noise bed with 8 s swells; 25 s; stems 48 kHz stereo; mixes = amix -> alimiter -> AAC 192k, 1080x1920 testsrc2 video, H.264)
measurement: all numbers below are MEASURED on the final files with `ffmpeg -i X -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` (Integrated / LRA / True peak) and on the per-mix gained stems X_voice.wav / X_music.wav (ratio = LUFS_voice - LUFS_music); see runs/07-loudness/make-mixes.log

seeded.what: too loud: integrated -9.8 LUFS (intended about -8; the -4 dBFS limiter needed to keep AAC true peak legal saturates before -8), 4.8 LU over target, 3.8 LU over the +-1 tolerance
voice buried: voice stem 10 dB UNDER the music (ratio -10 dB) at a legal integrated level

seeded.location: 4 ms 1 kHz bursts at 0.98 FS every 5 s (t=0,5,10,15,20 s), added after the limiter
seeded.what: true peak +1.2 dBTP (after AAC) at a legal integrated level

notes: Per-mix stems are 32-bit float wav so the hot L1 stems do not clip (first run with 16-bit stems clipped L1_voice.wav and dropped its ratio to 5.6 dB, a fixture artefact, since fixed).

AAC encoding overshoots true peak: a mix limited at -4 dBFS sample peak came out at -0.9 dBTP in the first run when its stems clipped; the final mixes limited at -3 dBFS measure -2.7 dBTP. Leave >= 2 dB headroom below -1 dBTP before AAC.
No fixture is a real recording; all synthetic, no licence issues.
